title: India Claims 17 Medals at Inaugural U-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championship in Lagos
excerpt: Indian fencers secure four golds, four silvers, and nine bronzes across individual events at the first-ever under-23 competition held on African soil.
body:
• India finished with 17 medals — four gold, four silver, and nine bronze — at the U-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championship in Lagos, Nigeria.
  • The U-23 category debuted this year, making India's young fencers among the first to compete at this level in Commonwealth competition.
  • The championship, held August 9–14 at Rugby School Lagos, marks the first time the event has been staged in Africa, with 16 nations participating.
  • India's haul underscores the country's rapid rise in fencing, following strong showings at the Asian Championships and Senior World Championships earlier this year.

India's under-23 fencing contingent delivered a commanding performance at the 2026 Commonwealth Fencing Championship in Lagos, Nigeria, winning 17 medals across individual events in a breakout showing for the country's young talent pipeline.

The squad claimed four gold, four silver, and nine bronze medals across épée, foil, and sabre disciplines, finishing as one of the top-performing nations in the inaugural U-23 category, according to The Hindu and The Impressive Times.

A Historic First for the Championship

The 2026 edition of the Commonwealth Fencing Championship carries two firsts: it is the first time the event has been held in Africa, and it is the first year the under-23 category has been included alongside the traditional senior and veteran divisions.

The championship, organized by the Nigeria Fencing Federation in partnership with the Commonwealth Fencing Federation, runs from August 9 to 14 at Rugby School Lagos in Eko Atlantic, Victoria Island. Athletes from 16 Commonwealth nations — including Australia, England, South Africa, Singapore, and host Nigeria — are competing across individual and team events in all three weapons.

"Despite global challenges, we are delighted by the strong participation this year, particularly with the introduction of the U23 category, which has attracted impressive numbers."

— Helen Dufour, Commonwealth Fencing Federation

Nigeria beat Australia to secure the hosting rights, a milestone that Nigeria Fencing Federation president Adeyinka Samuel described as historic. "This is an opportunity to showcase our ability to host international competitions and to expand fencing into more schools and clubs across the country," Samuel told KapitalFM.

India's Fencing Momentum

The 17-medal haul in Lagos is the latest marker in India's accelerating trajectory in international fencing. The Fencing Association of India has invested heavily in youth development over the past several years, and the results are now showing on the competitive stage.

Earlier this year, India hosted the Asian Fencing Championships at Pragati Maidan in New Delhi — an event the FAI used to give its rising stars invaluable exposure against the continent's elite. Indian fencers recorded top-25 finishes in multiple individual events there, with athletes like Prachi Lohan in women's épée and Sachin in men's foil showing the country is closing the gap with established Asian powerhouses Japan and South Korea.

In July, India sent a full squad to the Senior World Championships in Hong Kong, fielding 24 athletes across all six events. The team included experienced names like Tokyo Olympian C.A. Bhavani Devi alongside younger fencers such as Taniksha Khatri, Shreya Gupta, and Lakshay Badser — several of whom are in the age bracket for the U-23 competition.

What the U-23 Category Means

The introduction of the under-23 tier is designed to bridge the development gap between junior and senior fencing. For countries like India that have invested in grassroots programs, it provides a competitive platform where emerging talent can test themselves against international peers without facing the full depth of the senior field.

India's four gold medals across different weapon categories suggest the country's development is not concentrated in a single discipline — a sign of systemic depth that bodes well for the LA 2028 Olympic cycle.

Beyond Competition

The Lagos championship also features wheelchair fencing as a full medal event for the first time, after a successful demonstration at the 2022 Championships in London. In partnership with World Ability Sports, Nigeria launched an academy ahead of the competition to train athletes, coaches, and referees in wheelchair fencing — positioning the country as a leader in adaptive sports across Africa.

Nigeria is hosting wheelchair fencers from eight countries, reinforcing the Commonwealth Fencing Federation's stated mission to expand diversity and representation in the sport.

Looking Ahead

With the senior and veteran events still underway through August 14, India will be looking to add to its medal count. The strong U-23 performance sets a foundation for what could be a deeper presence in international fencing competitions in the run-up to the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, where fencing remains one of the marquee combat sports.

For Indian fencing, the Lagos championships validate a strategy of investing in youth and seeking out every available competitive platform — from Asian Championships on home soil to Commonwealth events in West Africa.
